correctness.rationale: For positive data T² applies g in each coordinate and T⁴ applies h=g∘g. The scalar h is increasing and maps into a bounded interval away from zero, so its trajectories converge monotonically to roots and it has no other periods. For m>1, the Schwarzian of g follows from writing it as a fractional-linear map of z^m; it is −(m²−1)/(2z²). The Schwarzian chain rule implies strict convexity of (h′)^(−1/2), so Rolle permits at most three roots; at criticality h′(w)=1 already, so two additional roots are impossible. Above threshold the signs at 0, w±ε and infinity give both outer roots and their signs; the paired-root multiplier q=(m sinh(t)/sinh(mt))²<1 also rules out a pair below threshold (two downcrossings would require an upcrossing at w). For m≤1 use the strict logarithmic contraction after entry into [g(b),b]. The product grid splits into the claimed cycles, with the two lines precisely the union of the saddle stable set and the central fixed point and the boundaries between the return phases; the diagonal derivative supplies the stated multipliers. Recomputed the critical cubic coefficient c=(m²−1)/(6w_*²) and the derivative K=(m−1)²/(m w_*) of h_b′(w(b)). Reciprocal squares give the signed limit 1/sqrt(2c) for four-step return times; dividing the fixed-point expansion by the nonzero phase offset gives s²/(b−b_*)→K/c, with the claimed square-root amplitude. The exact m=2 equations force uv=1 and u+v=b for the nontrivial pair. No numerical premise is used in these arguments.
residual_risks: Positive coordinates only. Both asymptotics hold for fixed m>1; the critical law counts returns of T⁴ and is not a uniform estimate in parameters or initial data.
